gates.notes: Loop ends when from >= horizonEnd, on an empty batch, on a short batch (< 2000), or on the first free slot; from advances by at least 1 ms past the last candidate, so it always progresses. Horizon is maxDaysAhead <= 365 (schema). Candidates are on a 60-minute grid, so at most about 24-25 per day (more only in DST repeat hours), giving about 8,800 candidates over 366 days, so at most 5 batches. Reads: loader 3 + per batch at most 2 (cap findMany, conflict findForConflictCheck) = at most 13 DB reads per request worst case. CPU: generateCandidates is re-run per batch from the new start and walks days up to the horizon, so total evaluateAvailability work is at most about 5 x 8,800 = 44k evaluations (Intl-backed, tens to low hundreds of ms); no per-candidate queries.

gates.gate: tenant scoping of every read in the batching path
gates.notes: Cap findMany has where.tenantId = input.tenantId (ctx.user.tenantId). Conflict read goes through appointmentRepository.forTenant(input.tenantId).findForConflictCheck. Loader reads pass tenantId. Per-batch windows are derived from candidates of this tenant's rules only. attendeeId is still caller-supplied (pre-existing) but the conflict read is tenant-scoped, so it cannot read another tenant's appointments.

isValidTimezone(rules.timezone) checked before any search; throws PRECONDITION_FAILED with the fixed exported INVALID_TIMEZONE_MESSAGE (no stored value echoed). Same code as create and reschedule. Removes the previous silent empty-result path.

appointment-settings.router.ts: arrow-function reshaping only, upsert still keyed on ctx.tenant.tenantId. appointments.router.ts: dropped a console.log in findNextSlot (reduces log noise; nothing sensitive was logged). Number.parseInt substitutions. packages/db/prisma/schema.prisma shows 3,624 changed lines but git diff -w --ignore-cr-at-eol shows none: line-ending churn only, no schema change. The migration SQL is unchanged.
Delta in apps and packages contains no secret-shaped strings or hosts; no package.json or lockfile changes. Not re-run: gitleaks, pnpm audit, tests (per instruction).

Cap-race waiver author is now Talysson (approved in lane modal 2026-10-17) per lead; I did not re-read the waivers file. Finding 3 is now tracked as gh #914, a debt-ledger entry and findings T8 per lead.

findings.issue: Interaction with #914: durationMinutes has no maximum. It does not enlarge the batch count or reads (candidates are fewer, since the policy rejects intervals that span midnight or leave the hours). But a value large enough to make the end instant an Invalid Date (about 1.4e11 minutes and up) makes Intl formatting throw RangeError inside generateCandidates. That is not caught and surfaces as an INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR (verified: Intl.DateTimeFormat.format throws RangeError on an Invalid Date). Authenticated, one request, no amplification, no data exposure; error noise and a misleading 500 only.
findings.fix: Add .max(1440) (or a policy-derived limit) to durationMinutes in findNextSlotSchema as part of #914, and/or guard in generateCandidates with Number.isFinite(end.getTime()). Also add .max(64) to attendeeId.

limitations: Manual diff review only. No gitleaks, pnpm audit, snyk, semgrep, trivy, build or tests were run (per instruction). The read and evaluation counts are derived by reading the code (60-minute grid, 5 batches of 2000 over at most 366 days), not measured; I did not time a worst-case request. The RangeError was confirmed with a one-line Node check of Intl, not by calling the router. I did not re-read the waivers file or the #914 / T8 entries; those statuses are taken from the lead's message.
